SMTO-WEB-0013 — The search server refused SMTO's connection test

GUID: 2b48ee02-afd6-4424-8499-bb78c2135111
Slug: provider-json-api-unavailable
Domain: WEB · Subsystem: web

What happened

  • SMTO's test search was refused by the search server (access denied). That refusal alone doesn't show why; the results format may be switched off, or the server may be blocking SMTO.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the person who runs your SearXNG server whether it blocks requests from SMTO's computer, for example with a sign-in page, an allow list or bot protection. An access rule on the server refuses the test in exactly the same way as a switched-off results format.
  2. Also ask them to confirm the server's search format settings allow the machine-readable results format that SMTO uses. SMTO needs that format to read SearXNG results, and the server may have it turned off.
  3. Then open Settings › Setup › Capabilities, select Configure Web, and select Test connection again. A new test shows whether the actual cause has been fixed.

What success looks like

  • Test connection shows Connected for that provider.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who runs the search server. Don't assume turning on the results format fixes every refusal, and don't reset passwords or keys without first checking why access was denied.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The SearXNG connection test received HTTP 403, which SMTO reports as provider_json_api_unavailable even though the status alone does not establish that JSON output is disabled.

What this means

  • The connection-test wrapper classifies every HTTP 403 under its retained JSON-API-unavailable kind, even without evidence that JSON is disabled. The diagnostic adds no retrieval. Read outcomes and retained receipts determine what evidence is available; an error does not establish the content of an unread source.

Why this can happen

  • The connection-test wrapper classifies every HTTP 403 under its retained JSON-API-unavailable kind, even without evidence that JSON is disabled.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect endpoint authorization and configured JSON formats; status 403 alone cannot identify the cause.

How to fix it

  • SearXNGProvider.test in src/agent_runtime/skills/web/providers.py relabels any 403 as provider_json_api_unavailable. Inspect the instance's access rules (reverse proxy, limiter, IP filters) and confirm search.formats in its settings.yml includes json, then run Test connection again; do not assume enabling JSON resolves every HTTP 403.
  • Check endpoint access rules and JSON output configuration using the recorded response; do not assume enabling JSON resolves every HTTP 403.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The same authorized connection test returns a valid JSON result after the actual access or format issue is corrected.

What not to do

  • Do not infer that JSON output is disabled solely from HTTP 403 or reset credentials without checking the denial.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic adds no retrieval. Read outcomes and retained receipts determine what evidence is available; an error does not establish the content of an unread source.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
